{"basis":"measured","fact_type":"finding","name":"MEASURED 2026-09-28 (static): four edge types are two to four different relations under one name, split by a property value on each edge — so the per-TYPE reading just declared is right for only part of their instances, and any rule moved onto readings would inherit the error","source":"three-graph primitives classification, 2026-09-28 (primitives repo github.com/sligara7/primitives, analysis/synthesis/reflow2-edge-readings-for-review.md and analysis/classified/reflow2/notes.md), items re-verified in schema and code","statement":"Found while building req:every-edge-type-declares-what-it-means, from the three-graph classification's review sheet (its medium-confidence rows) and re-checked against schema and code at origin/main 329a074:
1. CAUSES carries `basis` ∈ {observed, correlational, causal, spurious}, DEFAULT correlational (schema/inference.yaml:28). An unannotated CAUSES edge therefore asserts a correlation, and `spurious` asserts that there is NO causal link — while the declared reading says causes(+). edge_types_read_as("causes", …) returns CAUSES regardless.
2. CONTRADICTS with `alignment: supporting` means corroboration — the opposite relation — and two code paths filter it back out by hand (heal.rs:1950, report.rs:2253). Precedent: dec:idea-how-should-one-finding-say-it-corroborates-another.
3. AUTHORED_BY `role=approver` is the owner's signature on an ACCEPTED node (read by the intent-authority gate), but on a PROPOSED Decision it means the person was ASKED to settle it (report.rs:431, the assigned-decisions count). Same edge, same role value, two relations, told apart by the target's status. Roles were already made a set once because one relation per edge was losing facts.
4. INTERACTS_WITH is an umbrella: each `interaction` value reads cleanly (three as flows-to, `triggers` as causes); unset, it asserts only that some relation exists (its reading is `leftover`).
CONSEQUENCE: a per-type reading cannot be right for these four. Before any existing rule moves onto readings (the follow-up PR), a reading needs a per-value split — the classification scheme already has the field for it (`subtypes`, one reading per value of the splitting property) — and selection must honour it per edge instance, not per type.","subject_id":"cap:edges-are-selected-by-their-declared-reading","valid_from":"2026-09-28"}
